3. The plaint case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land was under the Nayabad Taluk of Azmat Ali Khan which was taken settlement by Golam Gafur Sawdagar and Azgar Ali by registered deed dated 20.02.1877. The earlier suit land was used as a tea garden and that subsequently the Government gave possession of some portion of the land in favour of the settlement receiver Golam Gafur Sawdagar and thereafter Government took possession of the remaining land and handed over the same to the Chittagong District Council (Chittagong Zilla Parishad); that the said, Golam Gafur being dead was inherited by his 4 sons Kala Miah, Asmat Ali, Abdus samad and Abdul Gani and 2 daughters Ammajan and Misreijan as the legal heirs of Golam Gafur and that Golam Gafur Sawdagar being died before C.S. operation the propperty of said Golam Gafur was recorded in the name of his son Kala Miah under C.S. Khatian No. 130 being dag No. 338 as the other sons and daughters of Golam Gafur Sawdagar were minor at that time and the C.S. recorded Kala Miah died before marriage   and as such the land recorded in C.S. Khatian being amicably partitioned was lonely obtained by Abdul Gani brother of Kala Miah and that the said Abdul Gani being dead before R.S. operation and the suit land was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 982 in the name of Noor Husain, son of said Abdul Gani; that the R.S. recorded tenant Noor Hossain sold out the entire R.S. recorded property of R.S. Dag No. 931 and 932 by a Registered kabala being No 222 dated 26.01.1994 claiming possession to have been transferred to Mokbul Ahamed and that the said property by a Registered Kabala No. 1744 dated 19.05.1948 was transferred to Haji Fazar Rahman and sale Ahamed sawdagar with its possession and the Sale Ahmed, Sawdagar sold his portion of the suit land by 2 registered deed being No. 3487 dated 02.10.1950 and 3488 dated 02.10.1950: and by another registered deed No. 3644 dated 12.10.1950 to Abdul Monaf Contractor including the possession of the land in question and that in the P.S. Settlement the suit land was recorded as P.S. Khatian No. 1208 and 1214 and the property in question was recorded their 8, annas share in the name of Haji Fazar Rahman and the rest 8 annas share in the name of Abdul Monaf Contractor and that the P.S. recorded owner Abdul Monaf Contractor being in possession of the suit land of the 8 annas property as mentioned above constructed pucca and semi pucca structures and developed the land in question by spending huge amount and that suit property within the pourashava the holding was recorded in the name of the predecessor of plaintiff, petitioner Abul Monaf Contractor and the same was rented out by him and that the holding tax of the Municipality was regularly paid by the plaintiffs petitioner in continuation of their predecessor and that the B.S. record of suit land was recorded in the name of Abdul Monaf Contractor as per his right and possession and that the B.S. record holder Abdul Monaf Contractor being dead the suit land was inherited by his legal heirs the present petitioners and respondent Nos. 5 and 6 and by way of continuing the payments of rents and tax as before being in continued possession and as such the right of possession was established. That it is further case of the plaintiffs that due to the introduction of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the right of the defendant-respondent No.1 the appellant petitioner the Villa parishad having been abolished and the rent receiving interest of Zilla Parishad do not exist and the plaintiffs-petitioners in continuation with their earlier ownership are in possession with their recorded right in the suit land through their predecessor-in-interest Noor Hossain in whose name the suit land was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 982 and that R.S. Khatian No. 981 was recorded in the name of defendant-respondent No.1 the Zilla Parishad. That though the defendant respondent-Zilla Parishad's right to realise rent from the plaintiff was extinguished it served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act upon the plaintiffs-petitioners which created cloud over their right, title and interest in the suit land and that the plaintiffs-petitioners failed to get relief in Other Class Suit No. 95 of 1992 as they sought irrelevant relief in the said suit and that some of the tenants of the plaintiffs-petitioners in collusion with the staffs of the defendant- respondent No. 1 denied the right and title of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs-petitioners were compelled to institute the suit against the defendants-respondents. 

 4. That the defendant-respondent No.1 Zilla Parishad contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter-alia, that by the registered settlement dated 20.02.1977 the predecessor of the plaintiffs Golam Gafur Sawdagar did not acquire any right, title and possession and there is no continuation of the same by the plaintiffs-petitioners and that the suit land as per R.S. Khatian No. 982 is not possible to be ascertained without local investigation and that the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs-petitioners in R.S. P.S and B.S Khatian were wrongly recorded having no legal basis and that the disputed land of R.S. Khatian No. 982 along with the land of R.S. Khatian No. 981 was entirely vested with the defendant-respondent No. 1 being the property of the Bharat Samrat without any rent and that taking the advantage of carelessness of the staffs of Zilla Parishad R.S. Khatian No.982 was wrongly recorded in the name of Noor Hossain as occupant of the suit land and that the suit land was never given settlement in the name of R.S. recorded (occupant Noor Hosain and no rent was collected from him being the settlement holder or the land in question and that the wrongly recorded P.S. and B.S. Khatian being in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs-petitioners on the basis of obtaining the same by way of registered kabala is not binding upon the defendant respondent and that the plaintiffs-petitioners filed Other suit No. 95 of 1992 in the 3rd Sub-Judge Court, Chittagong and the same being decreed against the defendant respondent the F.A. No. 39 of 1995 was preferred by the defendant respondent before the Hon'ble High Court Division which was allowed and against that the petitioner filed C.P. before the Appellate Division which was dismissed affirming the judgment of the F.A No. 39 of 1995 in favour of the defendant respondent and that possession of the plaintiffs-petitioners in the suit land was as the trespasser and for that no title was acquired by the predecessors of the plaintiffs-petitioners and also themselves and that the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata as the same issue was settled by the High Court Division which was subsequently affirmed by the Appellate Division and that the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. We have heard Mr. Md. Abu Siddique, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioners and perused the judgment and order of the High Court Division and other materials on record. The High Court Division having considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and materials on record found that in the registered deed dated 20th February, 1877 of the suit land there are some overwriting in a few sentences and interpolations and use of separate inks and insertion of a few sentences at the bottom of the deed. Accordingly the High Court Division holds that this deed is a spurious document which was totally overlooked by the courts below. The High Court Division also found that there is no material on record to snow that this deed attracts the suit lands as the plaintiffs-petitioners have not taken steps for repayment of the deed by way of local investigation. The High Court Division also noticed that the claim of acquisition of title on the basis of Exbt. 1 (Ka) to the plaint disproves the plaintiffs' acquisition of title in the suit lands. It has been noticed that admittedly the plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 95 of 1992 in respect of the suit lands which was decreed on 29th January, 1995. Against the said judgment passed by the 1 trial Court the petitioner preferred F.A. No. 39 of 1995 before the High Court Division which was allowed by the judgment and order dated 22nd January, 1998 and the suit was dismissed. Thereupon Civil Petition No. 447 of 1998 was preferred before the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division by the judgment and order dated 1st June, 1998 rejected the leave petition and thereafter the plaintiff petitioner instituted the present suit. The averments made in paragraph 5 of the plaint showed that the plaintiff instituted a suit being Other Class Suit No.95 of 1992 in respect of the suit lands. The High Court Division in the judgment observed that the learned Joint District Judge decreed the Suit No.95 of 1992 to the following effect-“নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদী পক্ষেও স্বত্ব স্বার্থ, অধিকার ও দখল আছে মর্মে ঘোষিত হল”. The High Court Division further observed that the courts below not only misread the pleadings and the evidence on record but also made inconsistent observations. The High Court Division found that the plaintiffs themselves admitted that they had instituted a suit earlier in respect of the suit land and lost up to the Appellate Division. The High Court Division in the judgment and decree in F.A. No. 39 of 1995 observed that the plaintiff could not file any paper to show that the alleged raiyat right of Noor Hossain, predecessor of the petitioners either on the basis of settlement or lease taken from the defendant-District Council and further the plaintiff could not file any rent receipt to show that Noor Hossain ever paid rent of the suit land to the defendant-District Council or the District Council ever realized any rent from Noor Hossain the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners. The High Court Division also relied on the decisions of the Appellate Division in Civil Petition No.457 of 1998 where it has been observed- "True but the plaintiffs could not file any paper to show how the alleged raiyati right of Noor Hossain on the basis of settlement or lease taken from defendant No.1. The High Court Division was well founded in law in holding that under the circumstances the plaintiffs have established a case of possession but not title. When they are in possession claiming raiyati settlement they cannot set up adverse possession either. They are not entitled to a declaration of title." The High Court Division having considered the above findings of the Appellate Division; in respect of the subject matter of the suit between the parties and admission of the plaintiffs in the plaint about the misreading of their earlier suit over the same subject matter and examined the question whether the suit is barred by the principles of resjudicata and whether the plaintiff can avoid the plea of resjudicata by adducing new facts. The High Court Division made detailed examination of principles of resjudicata in the facts and circumstances of the case. Having considered the proposition of law in details and the issues involved in the earlier suit and the present suit the High Court Division observed that in the earlier suit the plaintiffs claimed declaration of title and confirmation of possession and in this suit also they claimed similar reliefs besides other reliefs. Having considered all the aspect of the matter the High Court Division rightly found that the substantive reliefs in both the suits are for declaration of title an confirmation of possession in the suit lands. The High Court Division also found that in the instant case the plaintiffs arc admitting in their pleadings about the existence of decisions of the superior courts over the same subject matter and between the same parties. The principle of res judicata is applicable only where Court has in a previous suit or proceedings decided a matter in issue between the same parties. The object of the principle of res judicata as suggested by the expression itself is that finality should impart to judicial decisions and if a case is res judicata, it may not be reopened so as to be adjudged again. The fundamental principle of res judicata is that a question must be finally decided once for all by a competent Court forever between the parties.
